chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Zurara said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who traveled and left with his wife the maintenance for six months or thereabouts, then he died after one or two months. He said: 'The surplus of what is with her is returned in the inheritance.'
ai.seo_question: How is the surplus of pre-paid maintenance distributed when a husband dies shortly after leaving it with his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the legal status of pre-paid maintenance (nafaqah) left by a husband who dies shortly after departing, ruling that the wife retains only the portion corresponding to the actual duration of her maintenance, while the surplus reverts to the general estate. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that nafaqah is a debt or right tied to time, rather than an immediate gift, ensuring equitable distribution among all heirs. The ruling underscores the precision in calculating financial obligations within the family structure, a key theme in Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
